s1.syndrome_frame: Pruritic papular eruption of the extremities with a chronic time course
salient_findings: Rapidly spreading intensively pruritic papules on the extremities
Erythematous, annular papules measuring up to 5 mm wide
Asymptomatic brown flat papules on the face
key_facts: Female patient in her 50s
3-month history of symptoms
No remarkable medical or family history
No concurrent medications
Previous treatment with topical steroid ointments and oral compound glycyrrhizin tablets had no effect
Papules are scattered and erythematous
Palms, soles, and oral mucosa are not involved
Laboratory tests showed no abnormal findings
Skin biopsy revealed mild hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, and atrophy of the epidermis
Histopathology showed well-developed cornoid lamellae and individual cell dyskeratosis
Slight infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and eosinophils in the upper dermis

shortlist.label: Grover disease
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of pruritic papules with histopathological findings of cornoid lamellae and individual cell dyskeratosis

shortlist.label: Darier disease
shortlist.why_kept: Shares similar histopathological features such as suprabasal acantholytic dyskeratosis, although less common than Grover disease

shortlist.label: Keratosis follicularis
shortlist.why_kept: Presents with similar skin lesions, but less pruritic and without the distinctive histopathological features of Grover disease

shortlist.label: Pityriasis rubra pilaris
shortlist.why_kept: Can present with similar skin lesions, but typically involves the palms and soles, which are spared in this case

shortlist.label: Lichen planus
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause pruritic papules, but histopathology typically shows basal cell degeneration and a band-like lymphocytic infiltrate, which is not prominent in this case

raw.rationale: The presence of scattered, erythematous, annular papules, mild hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, and atrophy of the epidermis, along with well-developed cornoid lamellae and individual cell dyskeratosis, are characteristic features of Grover disease.

rejected.label: Darier disease
rejected.why: Darier disease typically presents with greasy, crusted papules in seborrheic areas and nail changes, which are not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Keratosis follicularis
rejected.why: Keratosis follicularis is a rare condition that primarily affects the follicles, which is not the primary site of involvement in this case.

rejected.label: Pityriasis rubra pilaris
rejected.why: Pityriasis rubra pilaris typically presents with orange-red scaling plaques, palmoplantar keratoderma, and often involves the face, which is not consistent with this case.

rejected.label: Lichen planus
rejected.why: Lichen planus typically presents with flat-topped, violaceous papules, and often involves the mucous membranes, which is not consistent with this case.
